_contract: The fleet's decision record - what a cold agent reads at boot. See README.md in this directory. Every decision carries the reason FOR it; every rejection carries the reason AGAINST and a reopen_when (empty = never, and empty is a deliberate act). verified_by differs from author on every entry - proposing and ratifying never rest in the same hand.

decisions.question: Which store should hold the fleet's decision graph?
decisions.reason: only store in the fleet with a seal, a signature, and a hash chain - a decision recorded anywhere else is asserted, not ratified
decisions.author: vishwakarma

decisions.question: Should the unique index on decision rows be partial or full?
decisions.reason: keeps the concurrent-seal race guard exactly as strong while superseded rows fall out of the index and accumulate as history
decisions.author: vishwakarma
decisions.record: nestor PR #31; proven first in apps/aristarchus

decisions.question: May the decision gate fail builds fail-closed?
decisions.reason: N1 bench (apps/aristarchus/bench/results/n1.json): at 0.90 the matcher cries wolf one question in five; at 0.95 it sleeps through half
decisions.author: vishwakarma

decisions.question: Does a promoted app ship its knowledge corpus?
decisions.commitment: no - ship the reader; the corpus stays with whoever grew it
decisions.reason: the capability travels, the wood stays: a semantic-search seam over injectable knowledge, never a bundled copy
decisions.author: vishwakarma
decisions.record: stores/README.md 'The one seam every store shares'

decisions.question: May a model verify, rule, seal, or publish?
decisions.commitment: no - a model may propose; only a person may verify, rule, seal, or publish
decisions.reason: the fleet's most load-bearing principle exists everywhere as prose (CLAUDE.md 0.2, intake_desk_spec 4.1, promote_check verified_by != author, Nestor's seal, the fourth-store narrative) and nowhere as a sealed decision - found by asking Nestor, which correctly answered that nobody ever sealed it. The intake desk paid the tuition: a router with a careful vocabulary contract still emitted unearned conclusions through the middle of it, because every rule was about storage and none was about authorship.
decisions.author: vishwakarma

decisions.question: May the field recording why a boundary was crossed be free text?
decisions.commitment: no - a closed set for writers, pinned by a test, permissive for readers
decisions.reason: convergent law: three sessions fixed this same defect independently in one night (homestead R-7 and I-13, Nestor #32 closed by #33, willow-mcp #280's event_type note) - a control nothing can check is a label, and a typo'd kind is not an event type, it is a row silently absent from every review surface
decisions.author: vishwakarma

decisions.question: Must a declared purpose be checkable rather than a label?
decisions.commitment: yes - a declared purpose is a control, and a control nothing can check is a label
decisions.reason: homestead's Purpose accepted any non-blank string, so 'x' bought the same lift as 'medical'; the fleet-level generalization is that any declaration which grants reach must be enforceable at the point it grants it
decisions.author: vishwakarma
decisions.record: homestead invariant I-13; operator note at sealing: possible prior art in willow-gate - to be reconciled

decisions.question: May a subject's testimony be published attributed under their name?
decisions.commitment: only under its own explicit scope (testimony_publication) - granting it never implies kb_promotion, and granting kb_promotion never implies it
decisions.reason: attributed testimony and de-identified structure are opposite movements: an oral-history desk publishes the naming as the record ('Names Given Not Chosen') while kb_promotion strips identity for a shared index - one consent must never quietly stand in for the other
decisions.author: vishwakarma
decisions.record: libs/subject-consent core.py (the scope's own comment); apps/intake-desk; operator note at sealing: possible prior art in willow-gate - to be reconciled

decisions.question: Must the governance chain head be anchored outside the database?
decisions.commitment: yes - hold verify()'s head somewhere the chain's writer cannot reach, and pass it back as expected_head
decisions.reason: rechain() proves the migration and the forgery are the same operation, so internal consistency alone can never answer 'is this the same chain it was yesterday'; a mirror without an external anchor degrades from 'someone else remembers' to 'someone else has a copy that will agree with whatever it now says'
decisions.author: vishwakarma
decisions.record: willow-mcp #280, PR #281; nestor ledger's expected_head precedent

rejections.question: Which store should hold the fleet's decision graph?
rejections.reason: SAPS1 has atoms and edges but no seal, no signature, no hash chain - a decision recorded there is asserted rather than ratified

rejections.question: Should the unique index on decision rows be partial or full?
rejections.reason: it is the documented concurrent-seal race guard; dropping it trades a correctness property for a convenience

rejections.question: May the decision gate fail builds fail-closed?
rejections.reason: the N1 bench numbers do not support it
rejections.reopen_when: a larger corpus or stronger encoder moves the 0.90-0.95 recall/false-match band

rejections.question: Should source code be eliminated in favor of AI-generated binaries?
rejections.option: generate efficient binaries directly, no source intermediate
rejections.reason: destroys the witness layer: source is the record, not the instructions - the only medium in which a second human can check the first; a model's derivation is neither deterministic nor reproducible, and opacity pools trust in whoever runs the model
rejections.reopen_when: generation becomes deterministic, reproducible, and auditable end to end

rejections.question: May a model verify, rule, seal, or publish?
rejections.option: the model reports 'corroborated by N sources' itself
rejections.reason: measured, not argued: the intake router's corroboration claims were wrong on 89% of an adversarial pass, including a source that explicitly denied a claim reported as confirming it

rejections.question: May the field recording why a boundary was crossed be free text?
rejections.option: close the set for readers too
rejections.reason: an audit trail must never refuse to show what it already recorded - historical kinds that predate the set must verify and extend (nestor #33's reader-permissive half)

rejections.question: Must the governance chain head be anchored outside the database?
rejections.option: the self-documenting rechain marker suffices on its own
rejections.reason: a determined operator can delete the marker and relink again; the marker makes a quiet relink loud, only the external anchor makes it detectable
